title: How the Client Connector performance troubleshooting runbook classifies slowness by pattern and routes it to its pages
aliases: Zscaler Client Connector Performance Support Troubleshooting Runbook

prose.label: Symptom classes.
prose.text: {{symptom-classes}} ISP UDP throttling is in [[zcc.troubleshooting.performance-runbook.udp-throttling]] and MTU is in [[zcc.troubleshooting.performance-runbook.path-mtu]]. The Internet & SaaS side is in [[zia.troubleshooting.performance-runbook]].

symptom-classes.statement: In its section on checking UDP throttling and MTU, which is marked Only Z-Tunnel 2.0, the Client Connector performance runbook addresses slowness from ISP throttling of UDP packets and from MTU mismatch reported by users on Z-Tunnel 2.0, and says an MTR trace alone does not identify these.

quotes: Check UDP Throttling and MTU (Only Z-Tunnel 2.0)
The following troubleshooting information addresses the major types of symptoms commonly reported by users facing performance issues using Zscaler Tunnel (Z-Tunnel) 2.0:
Slowness due to internet service provider (ISP) throttling UDP packets.
Slowness due to maximum transmission unit (MTU) mismatch.
A My Traceroute (MTR) trace alone is not helpful in identifying these issues.

os-pattern.statement: For slowness on a particular OS type, the runbook asks about an OS upgrade (test on the previous OS), a newly installed or updated third-party security or VPN app (disable its services), the Client Connector process allowlist, and high CPU utilization.

quotes: Slowness might be observed with a particular OS type, at office or at home, or when connected to any Zscaler data center.
Did an OS upgrade occur? | Check the behavior on a device with the previous OS or revert the OS on one of the impacted machines.
Did a third-party security or VPN app get newly installed or updated? | Disable the services of the app and monitor the performance.
Have the processes required for Zscaler Client Connector to function been allowlisted? | Revisit this allowlist to validate it.
High CPU utilization with Zscaler Client Connector enabled. | High CPU usage on the host machine could lead to performance issues.

all-users-pattern.statement: When all users of an organization are slow after a Client Connector upgrade, the runbook reverts a few workstations to the previously known working version and monitors performance; after a security patch or new software push it reverts that change on a few workstations.

quotes: Slow performance after a recent Zscaler Client Connector version upgrade. | Revert to the previously known working version on a few workstations and monitor performance.
Slowness performance after a recent security patch or new software push. | Revert the security patch or software push on a few workstations.

time-pattern.statement: For slowness at a particular time of day or day of the week, the runbook lists scheduled big data uploads or downloads and scheduled antivirus scans as possible causes.

quotes: Performance Issues Observed During a Particular Time of the Day or Day of the Week
Scheduled big data upload or download, which restricts the firewall or internet bandwidth.
Scheduled antivirus scans on the workstation, which restricts the CPU or memory utilization of the workstation.

office-pattern.statement: For slowness at one office location that is normal on a mobile hotspot or elsewhere, the runbook lists a Zscaler data center issue or maintenance and path congestion (collect Client Connector logs, escalate), and office router, switch or firewall issues (check CPU, memory, throttling policies and monitoring).

quotes: When the users connect from a non-office location or connect to their mobile hotspot from the office, the performance is normal.
Ongoing issue or maintenance at the Zscaler data center. | Collect the Zscaler Client Connector logs from the location and escalate to Zscaler Support.
Path congestion between office location and the Zscaler data center. | Collect the Zscaler Client Connector logs the location and escalate to Zscaler Support.
Check the general health parameters (e.g., CPU, memory, throttling policies, etc.), and check any network monitoring tools.

high-cpu-threshold.title: What CPU utilization the runbook counts as high
high-cpu-threshold.detail: The runbook lists high CPU utilization with Client Connector enabled as a cause of slowness and gives no threshold for high.
